messages:
maria-support: Hey team, FinOps reported payment-svc.internal.prod resolving to a public LB IP (54.23.12.5) intermittently since ~01:00 UTC, causing TLS SNI mismatch and 403s. Customer says it started after a cross-account zone change. Any obvious leads?

ben-eng-sre: That sounds like split-horizon / hosted zone overlap. Do we know if the VPC is still associated with the private hosted zone or if there's a resolver rule forwarding to on-prem?

maria-support: Customer confirmed they recently moved a hosted zone between accounts and added a forwarder for the on‑prem resolver (resolver rule id rslvr-az1f). They didn't change VPC associations on the RHZ during the move, but it may have auto-created a placeholder in the other account.

priya-dns: Can you paste dig output from a node in the affected VPC and from a public resolver? Need to see answers and SOA/TTL. Also check node-local-dns cache.

maria-support: Pasted from customer:

```
# on k8s node (10.0.12.45)
$ dig +short payment-svc.internal.prod @169.254.169.253
54.23.12.5

# from public resolver
$ dig +short payment-svc.internal.prod @8.8.8.8
<no answer>
```

They also ran `curl -v https://payment-svc.internal.prod/health` and got TLS cert for external.example.com.

kyle-oncall: That pretty much confirms split-horizon: inside VPC it resolves to a public IP. Could be a stale forwarder entry on our resolver rule that points to an old forwarder returning public answers. Check the resolver rule priority and the VPC association list: if two private zones exist (same name) AWS will pick the hosted zone with the matching VPC assoc, but forwarder rules can override.

priya-dns: Also check Route53 hosted zones in BOTH accounts for the exact zone name and any wildcard records. I've seen wildcard records in a migrated hosted zone return a public LB IP which then leaks to the VPC when resolver rule forwards to on‑prem forwarder.

maria-support: Customer ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name \"internal.prod.\"` and saw two hosted zones in different accounts. They said only one was supposed to be associated with their VPC.

ben-eng-sre: Ask them to run `get-hosted-zone --id <zoneid>` to show VPC associations. If the other zone has an association or if there is a resolver rule that forwards queries to an on-prem IP which itself resolves to the public LB, that's our culprit. Also check node-local cache TTL: kube-proxy / node-local may have cached the public IP.

maria-support: Customer ran checks, forwarded output:

```
# resolver rules
rslvr-az1f -> forward to 10.50.1.2 (onprem-forwarder)
rslvr-default -> system resolver

# hosted zones
Z1AAA... (account A) name=internal.prod. VPC associations: none
Z2BBB... (account B) name=internal.prod. VPC associations: vpc-0a1b2c3d (the customer's prod VPC)

# zone records in Z1AAA (account A)
payment-svc.internal.prod. A 54.23.12.5   # legacy public LB A record

# zone records in Z2BBB (account B)
payment-svc.internal.prod. A 10.0.150.22  # correct internal LB
```

They say Z1AAA was the old zone and should've been deleted.

priya-dns: OK two parallel zones explains it. DNS resolution priority inside VPC: Route53 private hosted zones associated with VPC should be authoritative. But because they have a resolver rule forwarding matching suffix to on‑prem, queries are hitting the forwarder which finds the old public record in Z1AAA (maybe cached onforwarder), then returns 54.23.12.5 to the VPC. That would bypass the local private zone.

ben-eng-sre: Mitigation steps:
- Undo or scope the resolver forwarding rule so queries for internal.prod don't go to on‑prem (remove that suffix match or lower priority).
- Delete or remove VPC associations from the stale hosted zone in account A (or delete the zone if safe).
- Flush node-local-dns cache and host caches: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=node-local-dns` and `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` on nodes if applicable.
- Check egress allowlist/firewall: ensure UDP/TCP 53 to the onprem forwarder is not blocked (we want to stop hitting it while we fix).

maria-support: Customer is hesitant to delete the zone immediately. They asked if we can temporarily force the node to resolve correctly without touching on‑prem rules.

kyle-oncall: You can add a Route53 record in the VPC-associated hosted zone with a higher TTL and set the record to the correct internal IP. That will make the private zone authoritative for the name. Also reduce node-local cache TTL by patching the config if you need fast turnover. But long-term you must fix the duplicate zone / forwarding rule.

maria-support: Customer applied a temporary A record override in Z2BBB for payment-svc pointing to 10.0.150.22. They still saw some clients hitting 54.23.12.5 for a short while.

priya-dns: That sounds like stale caches. Steps to validate after change:
- From a k8s pod: `dig +short payment-svc.internal.prod @169.254.169.253` should show 10.0.150.22
- If not, `tcpdump -n -s 0 -A port 53` on node to see where queries are going (to resolver or forwarder).

Example tcpdump snippet to share:

```
19:23:45.123 UDP 10.0.12.45:5353 -> 10.0.0.2:53  DNS 12345 q: payment-svc.internal.prod A
19:23:45.124 UDP 10.0.0.2:53 -> 10.0.12.45:5353 DNS Response 54.23.12.5
```

If you see responses coming from the forwarder IP with the bad IP, the forwarder is returning the stale public entry.

maria-support: They ran tcpdump and saw exactly that: queries go to 10.50.1.2 and responses contain 54.23.12.5.

ben-eng-sre: Root cause confirmed: resolver rule -> onprem forwarder returning stale public record from legacy hosted zone. Final fix path options:
- Remove/retire the old hosted zone Z1AAA (preferred) OR
- Remove the suffix match on the resolver rule for internal.prod so it doesn't forward those queries to on‑prem OR
- Reconfigure forwarder to prefer internal VPC resolver or purge its cache.

maria-support: Customer opted to narrow the resolver rule and asked for docs on how to check resolver rule priorities. I shared the steps to list resolver rules and the precedence notes. They also asked if TLS certs will auto-heal after DNS fix.

kyle-oncall: Yes, once the hostname resolves to the internal LB IP that serves the correct cert, SNI will match and TLS errors should disappear. Be mindful of client TLS session caching: clients with long-lived sessions may keep failing until sessions are renegotiated.

maria-support: Follow-up actions for us: 1) Share checklist for customers performing cross-account hosted zone migration (VPC assoc verification, resolver rule review, purge forwarder caches). 2) Recommend a guardrail in console to warn when creating resolver rules that overlap private hosted zones.

ben-eng-sre: I'll draft the KB and a short internal runbook for customers migrating private zones. Priya, can you add a DNS trouble-shooting snippet for our support playbook (dig/tcpdump commands, node-local flush steps)?

priya-dns: On it. Also adding a note: if forwarder is returning public answers, check for wildcard A records in the legacy zone (these are easy to miss and cause surprise leaks).

deploy-bot: Note: created support-ticket #S-472189 and linked migration checklist PRD-1332.

maria-support: Thanks everyone. Customer narrowed rule and flushed forwarder cache. They report resolution is now stable and 200s returned. Closing loop with them and will attach the KB we draft.
